title: [links 06/12] Derive an item's area through its projects on reads
body:
**Blocked by:** #1403, #1518, #1545
**Model tier:** medium

## Context

Model tier rationale: One read-side mechanism over existing relations with a fixed configuration list, batched through an existing batch relation read and verified with the seeded schema; no new storage or write contract.

Some values are never stored on the item at all; they are always computed from other items and cannot be overwritten. The first ones are an item's area, which comes from the area of the item's project (or projects), and an event's company, which comes from the company of its project. A file in the projects Web for client and Semprec iOS shows the area Work; change a project's area and every item in the project shows the new one with no further write.

Today Files, Health records, Journal and Companies have manual area relations (`Files.area` many-to-many without inverse, `Health records.area`, `Journal.area`, `Companies.area` one-to-one), and `Events.company` is a manual many-to-many with the inverse `Companies.meetings` (`seed/seedTenDatabases.ts`). Nothing computes these, nothing protects them, and no read says whether a value is manual. `Projects.area` is single-valued (a project has at most one area) and `Projects.company` is single-valued. The only derivation today is inside one item (`tasks.time`, `docs/adr/2026-09-19-derived-system-properties-computed-inline-at-choke-point.md`). #1403 adds the `links` read field; this issue adds the third kind of value to it. #1518 provides batched relation reads. #1662 then refuses manual writes where a derived value exists.

Decisions:

- Derived values are computed on read and never stored. They are opt-in with `include=derived` so list queries that do not need them pay nothing; `include=links` additionally lists them in `links` with `valueKind: "derived"`.
- The area of an item with several projects is the union of those projects' areas, de-duplicated by area id and ordered by title. A project without an area contributes nothing; an item without projects has no `derived` entry for it.
- The event company read is part of this issue because it uses the same mechanism (item to project to attribute); only the guarding of writes is separate.
- An area has `color` and `icon` in the result only if the Areas database has properties with those keys; today it does not, so both are `null`. Adding such properties is not part of this issue.
- A manual edge that already exists on an item with a project stays in storage and in relation reads; the derived value is authoritative in `derived` and `links`. Decided by the product owner: nothing is cleaned up or migrated.
- A Journal entry carries an area like any other item (decided by the product owner): with a project (the Journal-to-Projects relation `project` of #1545) its area is derived from the project; without a project it is the entry's own manual value.

## Task

Load `canonical-keys` and `testing`.

1. Add `backend/packages/data/src/derived/derivedValueSources.ts` (new) with the configuration list, one entry per database with a project relation, naming the project property: `tasks.project`, `events.project`, `files.projects`, `healthRecords.projects`, `journal.project` (the relation added by #1545). Use the database key constants from `seed/tenDatabaseKeys.ts`. Export it for the guard in #1662 and the invalidation job in #1710.
2. Add `backend/packages/data/src/derived/derivedValueReads.ts`: `getDerivedValuesForItems(client, items)` returning per item id `{ area?: { values: [{ id, title, color, icon }], via: "project", projectIds: string[] }, company?: { values: [{ id, title }], via: "project", projectIds: string[] } }`. `area` for every configured database, `company` only for events. Use the batch relation read from #1518 for item to projects and for project to area and company; resolve titles in one items lookup; a page of N items must not cause per-item queries. Trashed projects, areas and companies contribute nothing.
3. Expose it through the choke point facade and wire `include`: extend the `include` list from #1403 with `derived` on `item.get`, `database.query` and `view.query` (`schemas.ts`), attach `derived` to the item in `genericApplicationService.ts` and the REST envelopes, and parse `?include=derived` on `GET /api/items/:id` (comma-separated, together with `path` and `links`). `rows.ts`: add `derived?` to `Item` and `"derived"` to the link entry's `valueKind` union. When `links` is also requested, add an entry for `area` (and `company` for events) with `valueKind: "derived"`, `sources` listing each contributing project as `{ kind: "item", itemId, databaseKey: "projects", title, propertyKey: "area" | "company" }`, and `brokenBy` and `brokenAt` null.
4. Tests on the seeded databases: a file with the projects Web for client and Semprec iOS (both in area Work) returns one area, Work; a file with projects in Work and Home returns both; a task returns the area of its project; an item without a project, or whose project has no area, returns no `area`; a Journal day with project Web for client returns area Work, and a Journal day without a project has no derived area; an event with project Web for client returns `derived.company` Novak Web s.r.o.; changing the project's area changes the next read with no item write; a page of 50 items runs a constant number of queries; without `include=derived` the field is absent; `include=links` lists the derived entry; another tenant's areas never appear.

## Touches

- backend/packages/data/src/derived/derivedValueSources.ts (new)
- backend/packages/data/src/derived/derivedValueReads.ts (new)
- backend/packages/data/src/chokePoint/chokePoint.ts (facade method)
- backend/packages/data/src/chokePoint/valueLinkReads.ts (merge derived entries into `links`)
- backend/packages/data/src/index.ts (barrel export lines)
- backend/packages/shared/src/genericOperations/schemas.ts (`derived` in `include`)
- backend/packages/shared/src/genericOperations/rows.ts (`Item.derived`, `valueKind` union)
- backend/packages/application/src/genericApplicationService.ts
- backend/services/semprec-api/src/itemsHandler.ts
- backend/services/semprec-api/src/adapter/itemEnvelope.ts
- backend/services/semprec-api/src/adapter/itemQueryEnvelope.ts
- backend/packages/data/src/__tests__/derivedValueReads.test.ts (new)

## Scope

### In scope

- The read-side derivation of area (tasks, events, files, health records, Journal entries) and event company, and the `derived` read field with its `links` entries.

### Out of scope

- Refusing manual writes where a derived value exists: #1662.
- Realtime invalidation when a project's area or company changes: #1710.
- Filters, sorting and facets by derived area, and the search document: not planned yet; each waits for the filtering and search work to name the issue.
- Removing or hiding existing manual edges on items that have a project: decided not to be done (they stay; reads use the derived value).
- Adding color or icon properties to Areas.

## Acceptance criteria

- When a file has the projects Web for client and Semprec iOS, both in area Work, then `GET /api/items/:id?include=derived` returns `derived.area.values` with Work only; with projects in Work and Home it returns both.
- When a project's area changes, then the next read of its tasks, events and files returns the new area without any item write.
- When a Journal day has the project Web for client, then `derived.area.values` is Work; a Journal day without a project has no `derived.area`.
- When an event has the project Web for client, then `derived.company.values` is Novak Web s.r.o.
- When `include=links` is also given, then `links.area.valueKind` is `derived` with the contributing projects as sources.
- When no `include=derived` is given, then no `derived` field is returned.
- Reading a page of items runs a constant number of queries.
